Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Departures from Buyer Playbook and recommended pushback

## Overview

The Seller's cover note calls this "fair and balanced." It is not. Almost every risk-allocation term has moved to the Seller's preferred end of the range, and several provisions operate together to collapse the distinct protection regimes our playbook requires (Fundamental/Title, Fraud, Tax/IP, specific indemnities) into a single capped, time-limited, knowledge-barred general regime. The Disclosure Letter is more candid than the Update: it expressly confirms that the Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay payment evidence and bonus funding are all **absent**, which is useful for us. Nothing in either document binds us; none of the Seller's "negotiated" or "settled" characterisations reflect any Buyer agreement.

---

## 1. Liability regime

### 1.1 General cap – Clause 12.1 (Seller: 20% / AUD 4.8m)
**Departure:** Our starting position is 25% / AUD 6.0m. The Seller has gone straight to our conditional fallback figure.
**Reasoning:** 20% is usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None has been given, so the team cannot accept 20% in this round regardless of how the Seller frames it. Note also the Seller describes it as a "key negotiated position" – it is not; it is a unilateral proposal.
**Pushback:** Revert to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal the 20% figure is available.

### 1.2 Thresholds – Clause 12.2 (Seller: de minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k; excess-only)
**Departure:** Three-fold. Playbook is AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 basket, and **first-dollar** recovery once the basket is exceeded. The Seller's figures are 5x ours, and the "excess only" structure (a true deductible) means the first AUD 250k of loss is never recoverable.
**Reasoning:** On a AUD 24m deal with a ~AUD 3.6m single-customer concentration, a AUD 250k deductible plus a AUD 25k per-claim floor could exclude a meaningful cluster of mid-sized breaches entirely. The combination with the 18-month period and knowledge bar compounds the effect.
**Pushback:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / tipping basket (liable from the first dollar).

### 1.3 Time limits – Clauses 12.3 / 13 (Seller: 18 months; limitations apply to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise")
**Departure (period):** Playbook is 24 months; 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
**Departure (scope):** The default-to-all-Claims drafting is a hidden general-regime override. It would sweep Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, payment covenants and the Ironquay indemnity into the 18-month window unless we remember to carve each one out expressly. Drafting risk runs entirely against us.
**Pushback:** 24 months for general Warranty Claims. Reverse the default: limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and to nothing else unless expressly stated.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title claims (Seller: same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity")
**Departure:** Direct conflict with the playbook's separate regime: 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
**Reasoning:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. If title fails we have paid AUD 24m for shares the Seller could not convey; recovery capped at AUD 4.8m (or 6m) and extinguished after 18 months is unacceptable on any view. This is a walk-away-level point, not a trading point.
**Pushback:** Separate Schedule: Title/Capacity/Authority warranties – 100% cap, 6+ years, no basket, no de minimis, no knowledge qualifier.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance – Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 ("apply to all Claims of any nature")
**Departure:** No fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out at all. Playbook requires those to be carved out of **every** cap, basket, time limit, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provision to the maximum extent enforceable, and provides that no one on our side may waive this.
**Reasoning:** "Claims of any nature" is deliberately broad enough to argue that fraudulent misrepresentation is both capped and barred by the non-reliance clause. Even if a court would ultimately refuse to enforce that, we should not be litigating the point. Also, the exclusive-remedy clause as drafted would appear to exclude statutory and equitable remedies (misleading or deceptive conduct, rescission) which we should preserve for fraud.
**Pushback:** Insert an express, non-waivable carve-out: nothing in clauses 9, 12, 13 or 20 limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct by the Seller, the Company or any of their officers or advisers. Exclusive remedy and non-reliance clauses to be expressly subject to this.

---

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure – Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2
**Departure:** The Seller discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in" the entire data room, plus Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records". Playbook rejects whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure and requires specific, fair disclosure.
**Reasoning:** Whole-room disclosure shifts the burden of identifying problems to us and turns every undiscovered issue buried in DD-002 to DD-012 into a disclosed (and therefore non-actionable) matter. Para 1.4 (nothing admits breach, liability, materiality or that any consent/payment is required) is a standard reservation but, combined with 1.1, means the Seller both disclaims the significance of each matter and claims the benefit of having disclosed it.
**Pushback:** Delete 1.1 and 1.2. Disclosure is effective only if specifically and fairly made in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Documents may be disclosed by specific reference only. Delete "referred to in" (which captures documents not actually in the room).

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge – Clause 8.3
**Departure:** Blanket exclusion for anything the Buyer **or its advisers** knew, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records". Playbook: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier must reference named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
**Reasoning:** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard; combined with 1.1 above it effectively says no warranty claim can succeed in respect of anything that was in the room in any form. Imputing advisers' knowledge is a further step beyond market. The clause as drafted would also bar title, fraud and the Ironquay indemnity.
**Pushback:** Delete 8.3 in full. If any knowledge concept survives, it attaches to the **Seller's** warranties (awareness of named individuals after due enquiry), not to the Buyer. Confirm expressly that no Buyer knowledge, actual or constructive, limits Title/Capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

---

## 3. Conditions and completion mechanics

### 3.1 Bluefen – Clauses 3 / 6.3
**Facts:** ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%). Change-control clause 11.2 with conditions at 11.3. Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms **no final written consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied**.
**Departure:** The Seller proposes (a) reasonable endeavours only and (b) consent deemed satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent", irrespective of whether the 11.3 conditions have been met. Playbook requires effective consent AND evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer.
**Reasoning:** A conditional consent whose conditions are unmet is not a consent. For a 30% customer the risk is existential to the valuation. Note the Update says the consent "is addressed"; the Disclosure Letter contradicts that.
**Pushback:** Condition precedent: unconditional written Bluefen consent in agreed form, or conditional consent together with evidence satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably) that all 11.3 conditions are satisfied, delivered before Completion. Seller to use all reasonable endeavours (not merely reasonable) and to keep Buyer informed. No deemed satisfaction. Consider a long-stop date and price protection if consent is delayed.

### 3.2 Riverlark – Clauses 2 / 7
**Facts:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-of-control at 8.1; discharge at 9.2. Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge included.
**Departure:** Seller proposes release "following Completion". Playbook: current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; a post-completion release requires an irrevocable bank undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
**Reasoning:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal we must not complete with AUD 3.2m of secured debt in the target and only a promise of a later release. The 8.1 change-of-control term also means Completion itself may trigger default unless the facility is discharged or consent obtained.
**Pushback:** Pre-Completion payout letter from Riverlark; repayment by direct deduction from the Completion payment; executed deeds of release/PPSR discharge delivered at Completion (or at minimum an irrevocable Riverlark undertaking to release on receipt of funds, which still requires Amelia Frost's approval before we accept it). Price adjustment to reflect the payout.

### 3.3 Employee bonuses – DD-005 / funds flow
**Facts:** AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses, triggered by Completion and continued employment. Not in the funds flow; Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) are not addressed.
**Departure:** Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but has not put them in the funds flow, meaning they will be paid by the Company post-Completion i.e. by us. Playbook: specific line item or Seller-funded, including triggered on-costs; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Reasoning:** Bonuses triggered by this transaction are a transaction cost of the Seller. On-costs are likely to add materially to AUD 420,000 (superannuation and payroll tax depending on bonus characterisation and jurisdiction – to be confirmed by our tax advisers, not assumed).
**Pushback:** Either (a) Seller funds the gross cost plus all employer on-costs as a Completion deduction / Transaction Expense line item, or (b) the amounts are treated as Debt in the completion accounts. Obtain the DD-005 schedule and a calculation of on-costs.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP – Clause 11.1 and DD-004 / DD-010
**Facts:** Clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the room. The AUD 180,000 is **not independently verified in either direction** – we should not assume it is unpaid, nor that it is the full exposure.
**Departure:** Seller says the existing indemnity, limited to the SOW3 payment, is "adequate". Playbook: broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure.
**Reasoning:** The real risk is not the AUD 180,000 – it is that the Company does not own the SOW3 deliverables (and may be exposed to infringement or inability to exploit) until payment and assignment are complete. An indemnity for the fee alone does not cover loss of title to IP, third-party claims, re-development cost or associated revenue loss.
**Pushback:** Pre-Completion: Seller to procure payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay (the cure), with evidence delivered at Completion. Indemnity broadened to cover all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or to have been validly assigned, any Ironquay-developed materials, including third-party claims and remediation cost – outside the general cap/basket/time limits.

---

## 4. Diligence items where the Seller's characterisation should be tested, not accepted

### 4.1 Export/privacy incident – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 / DD-006
**Facts:** Download link sent to an unintended external address; possibly ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps). Unknown whether accessed; notification requirement undetermined; investigation preliminary.
**Seller position:** "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
**Our position:** Consistent with the playbook, we assume **no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand** either way – but we equally do not accept "not material" as a finding. The record does not support either conclusion yet.
**Pushback:** Covenant requiring preservation of all logs and evidence; completion of the investigation (including access-log review and recall/deletion confirmation from the recipient) with findings delivered to Buyer before Completion; ongoing update obligation; specific indemnity for Loss arising from the incident (including any regulatory notification, remediation and third-party claims) if the investigation establishes exposure. Do not price it in or demand a number at this stage.

### 4.2 Sandbar renewals – DD-008 / DD-011
**Facts:** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000). Seller: ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure does not say whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
**Our position:** Assess; **no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.** The Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported by the disclosure itself (para 8 expressly declines to say so).
**Pushback:** Request the three contracts and renewal notices, confirm timing relative to Locked Box/Completion Accounts date, confirm whether any amount is accrued or prepaid, and whether the contracts are terminable. Determine treatment (working capital / Debt / nothing) on the facts.

### 4.3 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
Disclosure Letter is careful to say the lease carries a notification obligation only, and the Mossvale assignment restriction does not require consent on a share sale. Both seem plausible but should be verified against the actual clauses; if so, a Completion deliverable confirming the landlord notification has been given is a low-cost ask. Not a major issue on current information.

### 4.4 Title – DD-012
**Departure:** Seller says title is "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012". Disclosure Letter para 10 itself concedes this merely identifies the source relied on and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
**Reasoning:** The share register is an internal document maintained by the Seller's own company; it is not independent proof. Playbook requires independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence.
**Pushback:** ASIC company extract and historical extract; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller for encumbrances over the shares; review of constitution for pre-emptive/transfer restrictions; Seller board minutes and any shareholder approvals authorising the sale; share certificates (or indemnity for lost certificates); confirmation no options/convertibles. Title warranty to remain in the Fundamental regime (see 1.4).

### 4.5 Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
**Departure:** Not settled. Playbook: Tax and IP terms remain **OPEN**; we assume neither unlimited liability nor any resolution. Rolling them into the general regime would subject tax exposure to a 20%/18-month limit, which is not a Buyer position and has not been negotiated.
**Pushback:** Reject the characterisation in writing. Tax (warranties and covenant/indemnity) and IP warranties to be separately scheduled with their own cap and period, to be negotiated. Do not accept default inclusion in clause 12/13 limitations (see 1.3).

---

## 5. Internal control points

- **No authority exists** to accept the 20% cap or the 18-month period. Both require Amelia Frost's prior written approval identifying the specific draft. The team should not trade on either in this round.
- **Post-Completion Riverlark release** likewise requires Amelia Frost's approval even with an irrevocable undertaking.
- **Fraud carve-out** cannot be waived by anyone on the deal team.
- The Seller's labels ("negotiated", "settled", "addressed", "adequate", "not material") are advocacy, not agreed positions. Our response should expressly reject the suggestion that any point has been agreed.

---

## 6. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m; 20% not available without Frost approval |
| 2 | Thresholds (12.2) | AUD 25k / AUD 250k / excess-only | AUD 5k / AUD 50k / tipping (first dollar) |
| 3 | General claims period (12.3) | 18 months | 24 months; 18 not available without Frost approval |
| 4 | Scope default (13) | Limits apply to all Claims unless stated | Reverse: limits apply only to general Warranty Claims |
| 5 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general warranties | Separate regime: 100% cap, 6+ years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge bar |
| 6 | Fraud / wilful concealment (9.3, 12.8, 20.5) | No carve-out; limits apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Express non-waivable carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance |
| 7 | Disclosure (Sch 7, DL 1.1–1.2) | Whole data room + public registers | Specific fair disclosure only; delete general disclosure |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Blanket bar incl. advisers and "discoverable" matters | Delete; no knowledge bar for title, capacity, fraud, specific indemnities |
| 9 | Bluefen consent (3 / 6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; deemed satisfied on delivery | CP: effective consent + evidence 11.3 conditions satisfied, pre-Completion |
| 10 | Riverlark (2 / 7) | Release after Completion | Payout letter; direct repayment from funds; releases at Completion; any post-Completion structure needs undertaking + Frost approval |
| 11 | Bonuses (DD-005) | Not in funds flow; "matter for Seller" | AUD 420k + on-costs as Seller-funded line item or Debt |
| 12 | Ironquay (11.1) | SOW3 fee indemnity only | Pre-Completion cure (payment + assignment); broadened IP ownership indemnity outside general limits |
| 13 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Preserve logs, complete investigation, updates, specific indemnity; no breach assumed, no number demanded |
| 14 | Sandbar (AUD 330k) | Ordinary course | Assess on documents; no automatic Debt/price treatment |
| 15 | Tax / IP | "Settled" under general regime | Open; separate schedules to be negotiated |
| 16 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent evidence: ASIC extracts, PPSR, constitution, authorisations, certificates |

**Priority order for the mark-up:** (i) Fundamental/Title and fraud carve-outs (structural, non-negotiable); (ii) Bluefen and Riverlark as Completion conditions/mechanics; (iii) disclosure and knowledge clauses; (iv) cap, basket and period economics; (v) bonuses and Ironquay; (vi) diligence follow-ups on DD-006, Sandbar, title verification, and lease/Mossvale confirmation.

I can prepare the clause-by-clause mark-up language and a diligence request list for items 9–16 if that would be useful.

Even if a court would ultimately refuse to enforce that, we should not be litigating the point. Also, the exclusive-remedy clause as drafted would appear to exclude statutory and equitable remedies (misleading or deceptive conduct, rescission) which we should preserve for fraud.
**Pushback:** Insert an express, non-waivable carve-out: nothing in clauses 9, 12, 13 or 20 limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct by the Seller, the Company or any of their officers or advisers. Exclusive remedy and non-reliance clauses to be expressly subject to this.

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure – Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2
**Departure:** The Seller discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in" the entire data room, plus Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records". Playbook rejects whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure and requires specific, fair disclosure.
**Reasoning:** Whole-room disclosure shifts the burden of identifying problems to us and turns every undiscovered issue buried in DD-002 to DD-012 into a disclosed (and therefore non-actionable) matter. Para 1.4 (nothing admits breach, liability, materiality or that any consent/payment is required) is a standard reservation but, combined with 1.1, means the Seller both disclaims the significance of each matter and claims the benefit of having disclosed it.
**Pushback:** Delete 1.1 and 1.2. Disclosure is effective only if specifically and fairly made in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Documents may be disclosed by specific reference only. Delete "referred to in" (which captures documents not actually in the room).

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge – Clause 8.3
**Departure:** Blanket exclusion for anything the Buyer **or its advisers** knew, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records". Playbook: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier must reference named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
**Reasoning:** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard; combined with 1.1 above it effectively says no warranty claim can succeed in respect of anything that was in the room in any form. Imputing advisers' knowledge is a further step beyond market. The clause as drafted would also bar title, fraud and the Ironquay indemnity.
**Pushback:** Delete 8.3 in full. If any knowledge concept survives, it attaches to the **Seller's** warranties (awareness of named individuals after due enquiry), not to the Buyer. Confirm expressly that no Buyer knowledge, actual or constructive, limits Title/Capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

## 3. Conditions and completion mechanics

### 3.1 Bluefen – Clauses 3 / 6.3
**Facts:** ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%). Change-control clause 11.2 with conditions at 11.3. Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms **no final written consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied**.
**Departure:** The Seller proposes (a) reasonable endeavours only and (b) consent deemed satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent", irrespective of whether the 11.3 conditions have been met. Playbook requires effective consent AND evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer.
**Reasoning:** A conditional consent whose conditions are unmet is not a consent. For a 30% customer the risk is existential to the valuation. Note the Update says the consent "is addressed"; the Disclosure Letter contradicts that.
**Pushback:** Condition precedent: unconditional written Bluefen consent in agreed form, or conditional consent together with evidence satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably) that all 11.3 conditions are satisfied, delivered before Completion. Seller to use all reasonable endeavours (not merely reasonable) and to keep Buyer informed. No deemed satisfaction. Consider a long-stop date and price protection if consent is delayed.

### 3.2 Riverlark – Clauses 2 / 7
**Facts:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-of-control at 8.1; discharge at 9.2. Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge included.
**Departure:** Seller proposes release "following Completion". Playbook: current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; a post-completion release requires an irrevocable bank undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
**Reasoning:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal we must not complete with AUD 3.2m of secured debt in the target and only a promise of a later release. The 8.1 change-of-control term also means Completion itself may trigger default unless the facility is discharged or consent obtained.
**Pushback:** Pre-Completion payout letter from Riverlark; repayment by direct deduction from the Completion payment; executed deeds of release/PPSR discharge delivered at Completion (or at minimum an irrevocable Riverlark undertaking to release on receipt of funds, which still requires Amelia Frost's approval before we accept it). Price adjustment to reflect the payout.

### 3.3 Employee bonuses – DD-005 / funds flow
**Facts:** AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses, triggered by Completion and continued employment. Not in the funds flow; Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) are not addressed.
**Departure:** Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but has not put them in the funds flow, meaning they will be paid by the Company post-Completion i.e. by us. Playbook: specific line item or Seller-funded, including triggered on-costs; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Reasoning:** Bonuses triggered by this transaction are a transaction cost of the Seller. On-costs are likely to add materially to AUD 420,000 (superannuation and payroll tax depending on bonus characterisation and jurisdiction – to be confirmed by our tax advisers, not assumed).
**Pushback:** Either (a) Seller funds the gross cost plus all employer on-costs as a Completion deduction / Transaction Expense line item, or (b) the amounts are treated as Debt in the completion accounts. Obtain the DD-005 schedule and a calculation of on-costs.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP – Clause 11.1 and DD-004 / DD-010
**Facts:** Clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the room. The AUD 180,000 is **not independently verified in either direction** – we should not assume it is unpaid, nor that it is the full exposure.
**Departure:** Seller says the existing indemnity, limited to the SOW3 payment, is "adequate". Playbook: broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure.
**Reasoning:** The real risk is not the AUD 180,000 – it is that the Company does not own the SOW3 deliverables (and may be exposed to infringement or inability to exploit) until payment and assignment are complete. An indemnity for the fee alone does not cover loss of title to IP, third-party claims, re-development cost or associated revenue loss.
**Pushback:** Pre-Completion: Seller to procure payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay (the cure), with evidence delivered at Completion. Indemnity broadened to cover all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or to have been validly assigned, any Ironquay-developed materials, including third-party claims and remediation cost – outside the general cap/basket/time limits.

## 4. Diligence items where the Seller's characterisation should be tested, not accepted

### 4.1 Export/privacy incident – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 / DD-006
**Facts:** Download link sent to an unintended external address; possibly ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps). Unknown whether accessed; notification requirement undetermined; investigation preliminary.
**Seller position:** "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
**Our position:** Consistent with the playbook, we assume **no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand** either way – but we equally do not accept "not material" as a finding. The record does not support either conclusion yet.
**Pushback:** Covenant requiring preservation of all logs and evidence; completion of the investigation (including access-log review and recall/deletion confirmation from the recipient) with findings delivered to Buyer before Completion; ongoing update obligation; specific indemnity for Loss arising from the incident (including any regulatory notification, remediation and third-party claims) if the investigation establishes exposure. Do not price it in or demand a number at this stage.

### 4.2 Sandbar renewals – DD-008 / DD-011
**Facts:** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000). Seller: ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure does not say whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
**Our position:** Assess; **no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.** The Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported by the disclosure itself (para 8 expressly declines to say so).
**Pushback:** Request the three contracts and renewal notices, confirm timing relative to Locked Box/Completion Accounts date, confirm whether any amount is accrued or prepaid, and whether the contracts are terminable. Determine treatment (working capital / Debt / nothing) on the facts.

### 4.3 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
Disclosure Letter is careful to say the lease carries a notification obligation only, and the Mossvale assignment restriction does not require consent on a share sale. Both seem plausible but should be verified against the actual clauses; if so, a Completion deliverable confirming the landlord notification has been given is a low-cost ask. Not a major issue on current information.

### 4.4 Title – DD-012
**Departure:** Seller says title is "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012". Disclosure Letter para 10 itself concedes this merely identifies the source relied on and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
**Reasoning:** The share register is an internal document maintained by the Seller's own company; it is not independent proof. Playbook requires independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence.
**Pushback:** ASIC company extract and historical extract; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller for encumbrances over the shares; review of constitution for pre-emptive/transfer restrictions; Seller board minutes and any shareholder approvals authorising the sale; share certificates (or indemnity for lost certificates); confirmation no options/convertibles. Title warranty to remain in the Fundamental regime (see 1.4).

### 4.5 Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
**Departure:** Not settled. Playbook: Tax and IP terms remain **OPEN**; we assume neither unlimited liability nor any resolution. Rolling them into the general regime would subject tax exposure to a 20%/18-month limit, which is not a Buyer position and has not been negotiated.
**Pushback:** Reject the characterisation in writing. Tax (warranties and covenant/indemnity) and IP warranties to be separately scheduled with their own cap and period, to be negotiated. Do not accept default inclusion in clause 12/13 limitations (see 1.3).
